title: TUI history pane reads the log only when it changed
lead: The history pane re-reads and parses `.slicer/log.jsonl` on every redraw; reuse the parsed history until the file changes.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** caching `State.history()` for the CLI or other callers; scrolling the history pane.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: s278's `history_lines` calls `State.history()` (`src/slicer/store.py:527`), which reads and parses the whole log, each time `draw()` paints the history pane (`src/slicer/tui.py`, the `view.shown == "history"` branch). The s278 gate measured about 20 ms per frame on this repo's log, and the log only grows. A redraw with no new history should not pay for a re-parse.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/tui.py`: cache the parsed history keyed on the log file's `(st_mtime_ns, st_size)`; a missing file or a changed key re-reads; a read error is not cached, so the pane keeps showing it until the file is fixed. `history_lines` keeps its signature and output.
- `CHANGELOG.md`, `tests/test_tui.py`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_HistoryLines_UnchangedLog_ReadsOnce` (patch `State.history` to count calls across two `history_lines` calls)
- `test_HistoryLines_AppendedEntry_ShowsNewEntry`
- `test_HistoryLines_MalformedLog_ShowsErrorInsteadOfRaising` stays green.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and watch them go red.
2. Add the cache. Mutation-check: always re-reading turns the first test red; never re-reading turns the second red.
3. Update the CHANGELOG.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full discover. `slicer check` and `git diff --check` pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
